learningObjective: Explain the role of IR verification in a compiler pipeline and identify when a verifier failure indicates a bug in the transformation rather than user code.

canonicalClaims.claim: IR verification checks that operations satisfy their declared invariants (types, shapes, region well-formedness) so that downstream passes and backends can rely on those invariants; a verifier failure after a pass indicates that the pass broke an invariant.
conditions: The IR framework runs verification before/after passes (default in MLIR).
The op invariants are declared via ODS/custom verifiers.
nonImplications: Does not imply verification catches full program semantic bugs (aliasing correctness, runtime undefined behavior).
Does not imply verification failures always indicate compiler bugs; malformed front-end IR is also possible.

misconceptions.claim: Verifier failures should be tolerated and deferred to runtime.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Verifier failures indicate IR that violates op invariants; running such IR yields undefined-in-compiler behavior, not a graceful runtime error.

misconceptions.claim: MLIR verifiers only check that the SSA graph is acyclic.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Verifiers check op-level constraints: operand types, region structure, attribute presence, result count, and op-defined predicates.

misconceptions.claim: Any verifier error blames the front-end that produced the initial IR.
misconceptions.whyWrong: If the front-end IR was verified successfully and a later pass produces failing IR, the pass is at fault.

misconceptions.claim: IR verification and runtime shape checks are the same feature.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Verification is a compile-time check on IR well-formedness; runtime shape checks execute in the deployed binary.

implementationFacts: MLIR runs verification after each pass by default (configurable)
ODS declares op traits and verifiers; custom verifiers are common for numerical / shape checks
Region invariants (e.g., single-block, terminator) are also enforced
performanceScenarios: Verifier passes are cheap relative to codegen; leaving them enabled during pipeline development catches transformation bugs early.
